claims.text: Protective oxide formation and retention in high-temperature HEAs is controlled by the interplay of sluggish diffusion and selective surface segregation of reactive elements such as Cr or Al.
This interplay promotes rapid formation of a dense, adherent oxide such as CrTaO4 or Al2O3.
The resulting oxide retards further oxidation.
The proposed starting material is a single-phase, well-homogenized HEA with an initially random elemental distribution and sufficient Cr and/or Al.
Reactive-element content or pretreatments that alter diffusion rates can be varied to test the proposed mechanism.
The relevant oxidation regime is approximately 1000–1100 °C for durations up to 200 hours under controlled oxygen partial pressure.
Sluggish diffusion limits outward cation transport during oxidation.
Sluggish diffusion produces controlled oxygen ingress.
Reactive elements preferentially segregate to the surface during high-temperature exposure.
Preferential reactive-element segregation facilitates formation of a uniform passivating oxide layer.
The disordered HEA lattice inherently decreases diffusivity of oxygen and metal cations.
Limited transport combined with reactive-element segregation selectively forms a stable, adherent oxide barrier.
HEAs with adequate reactive elements and sluggish diffusion will form a thin, continuous, stable oxide layer.
Such alloys will exhibit lower weight gain and thinner oxide scales than alloys lacking reactive elements or sluggish diffusion.
Conventional alloys or HEAs with reduced reactive-element content or increased diffusion kinetics will form more porous or more rapidly growing scales under identical conditions.
The hypothesis is limited to approximately 1000–1100 °C and compositions containing sufficient reactive elements.
Extreme oxidizing environments or alloys without the critical reactive elements may not exhibit the predicted protection.
An annealing pretreatment can increase diffusion by reducing HEA sluggishness.
The hypothesis is falsified if the modified alloy forms an equally dense, continuous, protective scale and shows oxidation resistance similar to the control.
